notes: The manual text lists an 82 ohm resistor, but the schematic labels it 220 ohm; 220 was used because the images are the authority.

The MKR WiFi 1010 is not in the picture's breadboard labelling convention: the image's breadboard rows are j-f on top and e-a on bottom, whereas the catalogue names the top half bank 't' with rows a-e. The top half is mapped to bank 't', with row letters chosen only to give each lead its own hole in the same column strip.

In the image the resistor's right end and the LED's anode leg share column 6, and the black wire and the LED cathode share column 8. They are given different holes in the same column strip (6t.c/6t.d, 8t.c/8t.b), so the electrical connectivity is unchanged.
The LED's bent, longer leg (column 6) is taken as the anode, connected through the resistor to pin 2. The cathode (column 8) goes to GND, matching the schematic.
The Micro USB cable (to a computer) is included as a part joined to the board's USB port. The other end is not shown in the manual.
The tutorial notes the built-in LED can be used instead. This graph uses the external LED circuit. A1 is only read in software and has nothing connected.
